note: Head-to-head and alternatives pages. The first five pairs were chosen from US search demand (treg keyword data, 2026-10-29): e2b, daytona, modal, vercel sandbox and cloudflare sandbox are the provider names people search for. InstaBox vs Lizard is an editorial pick (2026-11-12): two Firecracker providers at almost the same price that suit different jobs. Edges are our reading of the sourced feature rows, written by hand per pair.

isolation.why: Same Firecracker isolation and root on both, but only InstaBox documents Docker inside the machine.

sizes-regions.why: InstaBox goes to 32 vCPU and has L4 GPUs; Lizard stops at 8 vCPU but lets you pick US East or EU West.

lifecycle.why: Both pause with memory, but a stopped InstaBox machine keeps its disk, while a stopped Lizard sandbox is deleted.

snapshots-forks.why: Lizard snapshots and forks keep memory and running programs, up to 100 copies; InstaBox copies files only, up to 5.

storage.why: InstaBox includes 200 GiB of disk on Pro and keeps it on stop; Lizard keeps only a 1–50 GB volume on one node.

idle-timers.why: InstaBox pauses an idle machine by itself; Lizard has no idle timer and bills idle time until you pause or kill it.

reaching-it.why: InstaBox has public or private links, real SSH and a raw TCP preview; Lizard has private links only and no SSH protocol.

custom-domains.why: Neither puts your domain on a sandbox link, but Lizard supports custom domains for apps you deploy on it.

outbound-network.why: Lizard includes 2 TB per 30 days at no per-GB charge; InstaBox Pro includes 1 TiB and caps sending at about 50 Mbit/s.

keys-secrets.why: InstaBox can keep the real key outside the machine behind a placeholder; Lizard passes keys as variables any code can read.

ways-to-drive.why: Both have a dashboard, REST, TypeScript and Python SDKs, a CLI and a hosted MCP server; InstaBox adds real SSH.

built-in-agents.why: Both ship Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode (Lizard as one template each) and prompt them from the CLI; neither has a prompt API.

teams-accounts.why: InstaBox has a hard spend cap that stops machines; Lizard says there is no spending cap at all.

billing-models.why: Mirror-image plans ($20 vs $19) that come back as usage; Lizard is about 5% cheaper per hour, InstaBox stops billing when idle.

trials-free-tiers.why: InstaBox has a free machine that never expires; Lizard has a 7-day, $5 trial that needs a card.

company.why: InstaBox has a status page and a SOC 2 Type II report on request; Lizard lists SOC 2 as coming soon but offers a signed DPA.
